items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking lived experience
items.summary: The theme of this year's World Mental Health Day, held on Oct 10, is Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change. On its website, WHO states that the voices of people with lived experience should “shape the policies, services and decisions that affect their lives”. While these are laudable aims, they also serve to highlight the complex challenges involved in lived experience engagement and co-production, both within the field of mental health and beyond.

items.title: [Comment] Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: what have we learned from TRIUMPH-2?
items.summary: It is a general observation that the degree of weight loss obtained with GLP-1 receptor agonists is less in individuals with type 2 diabetes than in people without diabetes and similar BMI. Could this difference be overcome with the new triple agonists with superior weight-lowering effects? The TRIUMPH-2 study by Virginia Bellido and colleagues1 in The Lancet is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial of the effects of retatrutide, a triple agonist (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon), in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: [Comment] Closing the gap on mortality for adolescents living with HIV
items.summary: Despite major advancements in antiretroviral therapy (ART), a substantial mortality gap remains for adolescents living with HIV compared with the general population.1 Adolescents’ access to ART lags behind that of adults—approximately 60% for adolescents compared with 78% overall.2 For those who do receive life-saving therapy, inconsistent adherence to daily ART among many adolescents with HIV leads to viral non-suppression, increasing risks of clinical failure and death.3 The LATA trial, reported in The Lancet by Mutsa Bwakura-Dangarembizi and colleagues, was conducted in the four African countries in which most of the world's 1·57 million adolescents living with HIV reside; it offers hope that the challenges of adhering to daily oral ART for adolescents can be mitigated with longer acting injectable treatment options.

items.title: [Comment] Offline: Medicine for peace
items.summary: Thomas Hobbes (1588–1679) is most famous for his line in Leviathan (1651) that, “the life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short”. That proposition may have been true in 17th-century England, but, thanks to the evolution and expansion of health systems, it is not so today for many, although obviously not all. But abstracting that line alone is to miss Hobbes’ wider views about the nature of human being. He believed that without a “common power” ruling over society, our natural tendency is “that condition which is called war…of every man against every man”.

items.title: [Correspondence] Regulate prospective development of medical AI now
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing through medicine at a pace that regulation, ethics, and professional reflection have struggled to match. The prevailing assumption appears to be that if a technology can be developed, it should be developed—and that its place in clinical care can be debated afterwards. We believe this sequence should be reversed.

items.title: [Correspondence] The health literacy crisis in the age of AI: lessons from PISA 2025
items.summary: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) results should concern the health community.1 PISA does not measure health literacy directly, but it assesses several cognitive competencies that increasingly underpin people's ability to navigate health information. For example, in 2025, more than 760 000 students aged 15 years, from 91 countries and economies, participated in the assessment.1 The findings reveal a worrying deterioration in reading, mathematics, and science performance.

items.title: [Correspondence] Taiwan's path to hepatitis C elimination
items.summary: WHO has established a global target to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030.1 Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains one of the leading causes of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality, affecting an estimated 50 million people worldwide.2 By integrating a comprehensive screening-to-cure cascade, HCV elimination has become an achievable public health goal.

items.title: [Correspondence] Personalising maintenance after tirzepatide weight loss
items.summary: Deborah B Horn and colleagues’ SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN trial provides important evidence that continued tirzepatide is superior to treatment withdrawal for maintaining pharmacologically induced weight loss.1 The trial also shows that reducing tirzepatide to 5 mg offers substantially greater protection against weight regain than switching to placebo. However, the trial's mean effects might not fully convey an important clinical message: response to lower-dose maintenance was heterogeneous.

items.title: [Correspondence] How much can ASTRUM-006 tell us?
items.summary: Lin Shen and colleagues report improved event-free survival with perioperative serplulimab in PD-L1-positive resectable gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.1 The trial is valuable: it selects patients by combined positive score and tests a chemotherapy-free adjuvant phase. However, we urge caution before it is read as practice-changing.

items.title: [Correspondence] How much can ASTRUM-006 tell us? – Authors’ reply
items.summary: We thank Osman Bilge Kaya and Berkan Karabuğa for their insightful comments regarding ASTRUM-006.1 We agree that some aspects need further clarification.

items.title: [Correspondence] Colonoscopy screening and colorectal cancer outcomes: the NordICC trial
items.summary: Michal F Kaminski and colleagues report that colonoscopy screening reduced colorectal cancer incidence, but not mortality, during a 13-year follow-up.1 The response from the public health field will focus, as it always does, on mortality. We think this focus misses the point of the trial.

items.title: [Correspondence] Colonoscopy screening and colorectal cancer outcomes: the NordICC trial
items.summary: In their recent Article, Michal F Kaminski and colleagues reported the effects of offering one-time screening colonoscopy at ages 55–64 years after a 13-year follow-up of the NordICC trial.1 Their findings should be interpreted in the context that this trial of a one-time offer of screening colonoscopy was conducted in an era of widespread use of colonoscopy in clinical practice. Estimated reductions in the incidence and mortality of colorectal cancer were much lower than anticipated at trial design.

items.title: [Correspondence] Colonoscopy screening and colorectal cancer outcomes: the NordICC trial
items.summary: The NordICC trial1 should be considered in context with previous colorectal cancer screening studies.2,3 Four randomised controlled trials with more than 458 000 participants show consistent colorectal cancer incidence reductions of 18–23% and larger colorectal cancer mortality reductions of 22–31% with sigmoidoscopy (appendix).3 In the NordICC trial, screening reduced colorectal cancer incidence but not mortality.1

Nightjar wings reveal a trade-off between hunting slowly and traveling far
items.summary: The European nightjar (Caprimulgus europaeus) is a nocturnal migratory bird that travels between Europe and southern Africa each year. However, its wings are not only used for long-distance journeys. When hunting insects, the nightjar must be able to slow down, turn sharply and fly at low speeds. Researchers at Lund University have now shown how this trade-off is reflected in the bird's flight mechanics. The study is published in the journal PLOS Biology.

items.title: High Shoals Falls in Hiawassee, Georgia
items.summary: High Shoals Falls is a secluded waterfall. To get there you must access the trailhead on Indian Grave Gap Rd in Hiawassee, Ga. The drive up the mountain is exhilarating. Once you reach the trailhead, you begin descending the mountain. The trail leads you down into a small valley with beautiful scenery and several back country campsites. There are two waterfalls on the trail. The first one is Blue Hole Falls, the smaller of the two. The trail ends at High Shoals Falls where there is a boardwalk to view the falls from. The hike is a moderately challenging 2.4 miles round trip and worth every step.

items.title: A Purple Heart, A Lifetime of Service
items.summary: In 2007, Rafael Cervantes Jr. walked into a Marine Corps recruiting office with a friend who had recently taken the Oath to serve. Simply running errands in California alongside his friend, he had no interest in enlisting. While making small talk with someone in the office, Cervantes was asked if he would ever join. He answered with a sincere “no.” Their response changed everything. “Yeah, you probably couldn’t be a Marine,” they said. Eighteen years later, 1st Sgt. Cervantes is serving as the senior enlisted advisor of USMEPCOM 11th Battalion and St. Louis MEPS. For him, that responsibility is about far more than processing applicants. It is about helping people see what they are capable of becoming.

As part of a first-of-its-kind training rotation, Morley was one of 20 Royal Australian Navy Fleet Support Unit (FSU) sailors who trained in Hawaii to learn how to maintain U.S. nuclear-powered attack submarines. items.title: Quantum chip holds multiple photons at once, opening path to scalable memory
items.summary: For highly fragile quantum information systems, the ability to store quantum information is vital—but also challenging. Quantum information is transported in particles of light called photons, which often must be temporarily paused (or "stored") while other, slower quantum operations catch up. This storage must be performed on microchips as small as 1 centimeter (0.4 inches)—a distance covered by light in a few trillionths of a second. Storing photons for a microsecond would represent a massive leap forward for the capabilities of quantum chips.

items.title: Tiptree Jam Museum in Tiptree, England
items.summary: If you have stayed in hotels in the UK, you likely got a mini jam from Wilkin & Sons at your breakfast buffet. In a converted barn on the grounds of the Wilkin & Sons preserve factory in an Essex village, the Tiptree Jam Museum tells the story of one of Britain's most beloved jam brands. The entrance is marked by a long, retro-looking pole which was in fact the Tiptree Jam Factory's chimney from 1984 to 2021. The museum collection began informally in the 1970s when a member of the founding Wilkin family started rescuing old equipment and documents that had been destined for the scrap heap. It was not opened to the public until the 1990s. items.title: Gold Rush Cabin in Dawson City, Yukon
items.summary: No one knows exactly when Dawson City's Gold Rush Cabin was built, but historical records place it here by 1900 and suggest it may be somewhat older. Its earliest documented connections are to the Trading & Exploring Company, one of the businesses operating in Dawson as the frenzy of the Klondike Gold Rush was beginning to subside. Somehow, the little log cabin survived what happened next. As Dawson's population collapsed from the tens of thousands who had rushed north in search of gold, buildings were abandoned, dismantled, moved or disappeared altogether. This one remained and continued to serve as a home through much quieter decades of Dawson's history. By the early 2000s, however, survival was becoming considerably less certain. Further, a lack of understanding of structural discrimination relevant to the trial discipline can lead to erroneous conclusions. items.title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues
items.summary: Matsadaash staff allege torture and forced confessions after being held on charges of working for Muslim Brotherhood Egyptian journalists are planning a new protest in Cairo this weekend after six colleagues were charged with terrorism offences amid allegations they had been tortured in police detention. Last week, Egyptian authorities arrested the journalists, from the independent factchecking and investigative platform Matsadaash, accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and producing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood . Continue reading...

items.title: How a plant selfie in Colombian jungle led to ‘jaw dropping’ giant waterlily find
items.summary: Species with leaves large enough to be seen from space is already critically endangered – and plans are afoot to protect it A chance social media encounter has led to the race-against-time discovery of a new species of giant waterlily that has until now been hidden in the depths of Colombia’s jungle. But the plant, which is so huge it is visible from space, is already considered critically endangered. Continue reading...

items.title: Omnisolver: An extensible interface to Ising spin-glass and QUBO solvers: adding a distributed GPU brute-force plugin
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This software update extends Omnisolver with \texttt{omnisolver-bruteforce}, a first-class plugin for exact exhaustive search of QUBO and Ising instances on CUDA-enabled GPUs. The update contributes three components: packaging of the single-GPU brute-force kernel of [Computer Physics Communications 260, 107728, 2021] as a first-class Omnisolver plugin with a uniform Python and CLI interface, a Ray-based distributed framework that splits the search into $2^{k}$ fixed-variable subproblems and dispatches them across multiple GPUs and hosts, with a controller that gathers and merges partial results, and numerical stabilization of the fast \texttt{float32} ground-state path through compensated incremental updates, periodic exact energy re-anchoring, and best-buffer refresh. items.title: Strategic Governance of AI Models in Earth Science
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI foundation models pretrained on weather and climate data are increasingly fine-tuned to Earth science tasks well beyond weather forecasting. Their development and adoption are outpacing the scientific community's ability to evaluate them. These models are judged almost entirely by benchmark skill metrics, which measure how closely a forecast reproduces a reference product but not whether a model represents the physical processes governing the system it predicts. Forecast skill and physical reliability are therefore distinct properties. The distinction is most consequential under the nonstationary conditions of a changing climate for which these models were never trained. items.summary: arXiv:2610.10562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a parity-resolved spectral-connection construction for a one-dimensional Dirac particle in an attractive soft-core Coulomb potential. This defines parity-resolved spectral connection functions whose zeros determine bound-state energies. items.title: Inflationary Dynamics and CMB Constraints in $f(T,L_m)$ gravity
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate slow-roll inflation in a modified teleparallel framework with a non-minimal coupling between torsion and the matter sector. Focusing on Starobinsky-type plateau inflation, we derive the modified background dynamics and the corresponding slow-roll observables, and examine how the gravitational couplings affect the scalar spectral index, tensor-to-scalar ratio, and running of the spectral index. The model continuously recovers the standard Starobinsky scenario in the appropriate weak-coupling limit, while the matter--geometry coupling produces a non-monotonic modification of the inflationary predictions. items.title: Collapse and causality in generalised trace dynamics: record selection in Connes time and the causal consistency of emergent records
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamical wave-function collapse must not violate causality: a record selected "now" has no frame-independent meaning, and a nonlinear law can let distant observers signal. The hypersurface question is then not posed where selection happens; it returns as the requirement that emergent records do not signal. items.title: Partially Thermalized eV-Scale Sterile Neutrinos in Dynamical Dark Energy and Non-Flat Cosmologies
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate cosmological constraints on a $(3+1)$ neutrino framework containing an additional partially thermalized, eV-scale sterile neutrino alongside the three active species. Rather than assuming full thermalization, we allow the sterile abundance to vary independently through its physical mass $m_s$ and contribution $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ to the effective number of relativistic species. The sterile state is modeled as a thermally distributed non-cold relic with a temperature below that of the active-neutrino background. We consider flat and non-flat $\Lambda$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM cosmologies, all including the same $(3+1)\nu$ sector. The models are constrained using Planck 2018 CMB data, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae, a conservative compilation of $f\sigma_8$ measurements, and the recent H0DN. items.title: A Sign in Space part 2, a new simulated First Contact scenario engaging the global scientific SETI network, and integrating deep space technologies into SETI search
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence programme aims to find evidence of extraterrestrial intelligence. SETI scientists pursue this objective by searching for technosignatures primarily in the radio or optical spectrum. The IAA SETI Committee has been developing protocols to offer guidelines in case of an actual extraterrestrial signal reception. These protocols establish procedures to confirm the authenticity of the signal and its actual extraterrestrial nature, as well as the committee's role in managing the discovery in relation to the scientific community and the general public, targeting scientific queries in relation to the management and development of equipment and methodologies employed in current SETI search. items.title: When quantum field theory kicks in: the relation between matter, gravity and energy
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The existence of energy is the main criterion for (i) providing a common core to the materiality of all types of classical matter and (ii) denying that the gravitational field of General Relativity is a type of matter. Extending this criterion to quantum field theory, though formally straightforward, carries new conceptual consequences for the interpretation of gravity. items.title: Kinetic Reduction and Hydrodynamics under Time-Dependent Helical Symmetry
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Translational and helical symmetries provide idealized descriptions of many flows encountered in nature and engineering. While translationally symmetric flows have been extensively studied within kinetic and continuum frameworks, the corresponding connection between microscopic dynamics and continuum behaviour for helical flows is less developed. Here, we investigate this connection for a dilute gas with time-dependent helical symmetry. Using the objective molecular dynamics framework, we derive a reduced Boltzmann equation that retains radial variations while preserving the classical collision operator under helical symmetry. Formal hydrodynamic expansions then yield the corresponding Euler and Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations. items.title: Propagation-Invariant Transmission Eigenmodes in Weakly Scattering Media
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Propagation-invariant beams (PIBs) with annular angular spectra preserve their transverse intensity structure over extended propagation distances. Here, we investigate whether scattering invariant modes (SIMs) can simultaneously exhibit scattering and propagation invariance. We measure free-space and sample transmission matrices (TMs) in an orthonormal annular basis for weak, moderate, and strong scattering media and identify localized SIMs (LSIMs) whose angular spectra remain predominantly confined to one or a few neighboring rings. Under weak scattering, 75 of the 128 SIMs considered for annular localization satisfy this criterion, with LSIMs exhibiting Bessel-like propagation. items.title: Photoluminescence study of Vanadium in 4H- and 6H- Silicon Carbide
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Point defects with optically addressable spin states are a key building block for quantum networks, but few solid-state emitters combine a spin-photon interface with emission in the low-loss telecommunications band. Vanadium (V4+) defects in silicon carbide (SiC) meet this requirement, emitting zero-phonon lines (ZPLs) throughout the telecom O-band in both the 4H- and 6H-SiC polytypes while retaining an addressable electron and nuclear spin system [1,2]. Although the orbital and spin structure of these defects has been characterized in detail, the polarization selection rules have not been fully mapped experimentally. items.title: Fault-conditioned Seismic Image Generation using Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Modeling and Neural Style Transfer
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Seismic data augmentation is critical for training robust deep learning (DL) models for fault detection and characterization, yet conventional approaches remain inadequate. Geometric transforms, e.g., flips or rotations, and noise injection fail to capture realistic seismic textures, while physics-based forward modeling is computationally expensive and often poorly aligned with the statistical characteristics of field data. We present a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) framework that learns the high-dimensional distribution of seismic images directly from field data via iterative noise injection and learned denoising. items.title: A critical-layer instability of structural acoustic wall modes in a two-flexible-plate channel with Poiseuille flow: closed-form low-Mach corrections and parity-protected absorption
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A compressible fluid column between two thin elastic plates carrying plane Poiseuille flow supports discrete structural-acoustic wall modes. This paper analyses their coupled dispersion and reports a flow-induced instability. items.title: Technical Preparations for the First Carbon-Ion Therapy Facility in the United States
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) provides greater biological effectiveness than conventional photon therapy because of its high linear energy transfer and its ability to induce complex DNA damage. Mayo Clinic Florida is developing the first CIRT facility in the United States, using a synchrotron-based system with dose-driven continuous scanning (DDCS). Although DDCS improves delivery efficiency by keeping the beam on during spot transitions, it also creates the challenge of accurately modeling the dose delivered during beam motion (move dose), which is not fully addressed in current treatment planning systems. items.summary: arXiv:2610.10830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials have become indispensable tools in atomistic simulations. The most popular models rely heavily on physical priors, such as locality, smoothness and symmetry, that are assumed to improve the accuracy and transferability of the trained models. However, recent evidence suggests that, in the data-rich regime, unconstrained models that learn symmetry from the data can achieve very competitive accuracy and computational efficiency, without sacrificing stability and generalization power. items.title: Optimal Diffractive Focusing of Vortex Beams
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate diffractive ring focusing of paraxial beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) through a finite circular aperture as a variational optimization problem. For a fixed topological charge, we determine the real-valued radial pupil that maximizes the intensity at a prescribed ring radius and propagation distance under a normalization constraint on the input field. The resulting problem admits an exact analytical solution: the optimal pupil combines the familiar Fresnel phase structure with an OAM-dependent Bessel radial modulation, and the associated eigenvalue yields a rigorous upper bound on the achievable ring intensity. items.title: Localized, unstable, and entangled: Exploring `Us vs. Them' bias in Large Language Models
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit us-vs.-them bias: A behavioral asymmetry in which prompts framed around an ingroup (``we''/``us'') receive systematically more positive continuations than matched prompts framed around an outgroup (``they''/``them''). Using Edge Attribution Patching (EAP), we localize this behavior to directed circuits in GPT-2 Small, GPT-2 Large, Llama-2 7B, and Llama-3 8B. Across models, high-attribution edges are sparse and concentrated primarily in middle-to-late layers, while ingroup- and outgroup-related pathways are only partially overlapping and reorganize under fine-tuning. items.title: Ab Initio Investigation of Excited States and Absorption Spectra of Small Mercury Clusters (Hg$_{2-5}$)
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a systematic \textit{ab initio} investigation of the excited states and absorption spectra of small mercury clusters (Hg$_{\mathrm{2-5}}$). Benchmarking multi-reference configuration interaction (MR-CISD) and equation-of-motion coupled-cluster (EOM-CCSD) methods shows that EOM-CCSD/aug-cc-PVTZ-PP reproduces atomic excitation energies within $\pm$500 cm$^{-1}$ of experiment, whereas MR-CISD deviates by about $\pm$1100 cm$^{-1}$. For the mercury dimer, EOM-CCSD potential energy curves yield absorption bands in excellent agreement with experimental transitions, while asymptotic excitation energies closely match atomic references. items.title: An ecology of participation for fusion energy development
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decisions that will shape future fusion facilities, including the production of waste, the management of tritium, the achievement of safety, and impacts on land, water, and local communities, are increasingly becoming sociotechnical in nature. For prior energy technologies, fission among them, such decisions were made top-down and met sustained public opposition. Research shows such opposition is rarely a deficit of public understanding and is instead rooted in place-specific environmental, health, sociocultural, and economic concerns and in distrust of how technologies are selected and sited. items.title: Adapting Appearance-Based Gaze Estimation to Narrow-Range, Long-Duration Screen Viewing
items.summary: arXiv:2610.11036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Appearance-based gaze estimation offers a low-cost alternative to infrared eye tracking for screen-based behavioral and clinical applications, however existing models are typically developed for wide ranges of gaze angle and head pose. Prolonged screen viewing presents a distinct regime in which gaze remains near the screen center, head motion is limited, and calibration drift accumulates over time. In this work, we benchmark six published estimators along with a proposed differential-gaze model on 140 long-duration facial video recordings with synchronized eye tracking under subject-disjoint evaluation and a common budget of calibration frames. items.title: Skeleton-Guided Progressive Test-Time Adaptation for Thin Curvilinear Structures
items.summary: arXiv:2610.11104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate segmentation of thin curvilinear structures is vital for various real-world applications, from vessel analysis to road extraction. Yet their intricate geometry makes even minor pixel-wise errors enough to break the global topology, and this structural fragility turns severe domain shifts into catastrophic failures. The difficulty is most acute under cross-modality gaps, where the imaging process itself differs fundamentally between source and target. While test-time adaptation (TTA) offers a practical source-free remedy, existing methods adapt feature statistics and confidence, neither of which constrains connectivity, and thus degrade under such extreme gaps. items.summary: arXiv:2610.11144v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Single-image nutrition estimation can fail silently when visible foods are missed. Even when a food is correctly identified, its proposed region may not support portion estimation. We propose a framework that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to inventory visible foods and separately verify food identity and whether each proposed 2D region supports portion estimation. One whole-image review uses these verification results to identify unresolved gaps and omitted foods, triggering at most one targeted recovery pass. Recovered regions are re-verified without access to the recovery prompt, then reconciled into a final item set for nutrition estimation. The framework requires no task-specific fine-tuning. items.title: A Unified Score Matching Paradigm for Video Anomaly Detection and Anticipation
items.summary: arXiv:2610.11149v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video anomaly detection (VAD) is a fundamental and safety-critical task in computer vision. Recent generative approaches detect anomalies from a distributional perspective, but remain limited by local anomaly modes. Meanwhile, video anomaly anticipation (VAA), as a proactive extension beyond post-hoc detection, introduces additional challenges. In particular, the contrastive inference paradigm in VAD, which relies on ground-truth frames, is not applicable to VAA, hindering its development. items.summary: arXiv:2610.11232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kikuchi lines and bands in reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) carry information on crystal geometry and electron scattering, but are often obscured by intense diffraction streaks. items.title: Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization via Complex-Valued Fusion
items.summary: arXiv:2610.11846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization (OV-AVEL) labels each video segment with an event class, including classes that were never seen during training. Existing methods then collapse this pair into a single scalar score with a fixed rule (geometric mean, weighted average) before taking the argmax. items.title: LVS: Local View Synthesis from Relative Camera Pose by Reusing Previous Views
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12127v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interactive scene exploration requires frequent view updates, although small camera motions preserve much of the visible content. Conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting nevertheless renders each target view, leaving this image overlap unexploited. Reusing rendered images offers an alternative. Geometric warping alone cannot recover newly exposed content and remains sensitive to depth errors. We propose a per-scene framework that replaces repeated scene rendering for nearby views with relative-pose-guided RGB-D image reuse. Geometric warping uses depth and relative pose to transport source content, while a lightweight multiscale network predicts RGB residuals to correct artifacts and infer missing appearance. items.title: VesselSDF: Distance Field Priors for Vascular Network Reconstruction
items.summary: arXiv:2506.16556v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate segmentation of vascular networks from sparse CT scan slices remains a significant challenge in medical imaging, particularly due to the thin, branching nature of vessels and the inherent sparsity between imaging planes. Existing deep learning approaches, based on binary voxel classification, often struggle with structural continuity and geometric fidelity. To address this challenge, we present VesselSDF, a novel framework that leverages signed distance fields (SDFs) for robust vessel reconstruction. items.title: Distribution-Aligned Representation Adaptation for DJSCC over Hybrid Wireless-Wired Networks
items.summary: arXiv:2510.13422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep joint source-channel coding (DJSCC) has emerged as a robust alternative to traditional separate coding for communications through wireless channels. Existing DJSCC approaches focus primarily on point-to-point wireless communication scenarios, while neglecting end-to-end communication efficiency in hybrid wireless-wired networks such as 5G and 6G communication systems. Considerable redundancy in DJSCC symbols against wireless channels becomes inefficient for long-distance wired transmission. Furthermore, DJSCC symbols must adapt to the varying transmission rate of the wired network to avoid congestion. items.summary: arXiv:2602.23833v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automated identification of DICOM image series is essential for large-scale medical image analysis, quality control, protocol harmonization, and reliable downstream processing. However, DICOM series classification remains challenging due to heterogeneous slice content, variable series length, and entirely missing, incomplete or inconsistent DICOM metadata. (i) Images and metadata are encoded with modality-aware modules and fused using a bi-directional cross-modal attention mechanism. items.title: SCI-Mamba: Unsupervised Learning based Low-Light Image Enhancement for Non-Cooperative Spacecraft
items.summary: arXiv:2607.08033v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-light visual perception acts as the core visual foundation for on-orbit servicing missions targeting non-cooperative spacecraft, supporting autonomous rendezvous, pose estimation, component detection and robotic capture operations. Spaceborne imagery suffers from severe low-light degradation, while the extreme scarcity of paired normal/low-light space samples severely limits the generalization capacity of supervised enhancement algorithms. To address this practical bottleneck, this paper proposes SCI-Mamba, an unsupervised enhancement network for low-light orbital spacecraft observations. items.summary: arXiv:2609.08081v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Background: This study evaluated interreader agreement and longitudinal performance of MRI methods for knee cartilage volume, thickness, and defect-area quantification. items.title: The segmentation ceiling: why explicit left-ventricular masks do not improve learned ejection-fraction regression
items.summary: arXiv:2609.19730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate estimation of left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) from echocardiography is central to cardiovascular care, and deep learning enables automated EF prediction from echocardiographic video. Because EF is clinically derived from left-ventricular (LV) volumes, a widely held intuition is that explicit LV segmentation should improve prediction. items.title: An Explainable Header-Centric Framework for Large-Scale Semantic Table Interpretation and Data Quality Assessment
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge Graph (KG) quality depends not only on downstream graph validation, but also on the quality of tabular metadata used before integration. In metadata-only Semantic Table Interpretation (STI), where cell values are unavailable, noisy, or unsuitable, column headers become a critical source of semantic evidence for traceable KG preparation. We present an explainable, header-centric framework for metadata-only Column Type Annotation (CTA) and Data Quality Assessment (DQA). The framework maps headers to 39 interpretable FinalFormat types using curated lexical resources and preserves token-level traceability through SourceKeywords. items.title: Synthesis Through Simulation: Generating Coherent Enterprise Data via Scalable Agent-System Interaction
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-calling agents have become central to enterprise AI, yet training and evaluating them at scale remains severely constrained due to business and legal restrictions on enterprise systems, data, and database schemas. Tabular data synthesis offers a natural alternative, but its effectiveness is fundamentally limited by structural validity and schema availability, while procedure-based approaches yield the opposite weakness, typically lacking distributional fidelity without per-domain authoring. We introduce **Synthesis Through Simulation** (STS), a **schema--free** data synthesis paradigm in which an LLM agent generates data by executing operations against policy-enforcing APIs within simulated enterprise environments. items.title: Agent-Controlled Forgetting for Tool-Using Agents: Reversible Context Curation in Practice
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using agents repeatedly carry observations whose useful content can be much smaller than their original payload. items.title: It All Comes Together in Chattanooga
items.summary: Chattanooga may be best known for its natural beauty, surrounded by mountains, valleys, and the Tennessee River. This charming Appalachian city is also home to annual music festivals like the IBMA World of Bluegrass and the 3 Sisters Bluegrass Festival . items.title: Museo Torre del Vino in Socuéllamos, Spain
items.summary: In Socuéllamos, you can climb a tower without ever leaving the world of wine. The Museo Torre del Vino occupies the town’s former railway station, but its most eye-catching feature is the improbable tower rising above it—a vertical tribute to the grape in the heart of La Mancha. Opened in 2014, the museum explores Socuéllamos’s long relationship with viticulture, from grape cultivation and traditional winemaking to the science and rituals of tasting. Interactive displays and exhibitions make the subject considerably more entertaining than it sounds, while workshops involving aromas, wine painting, and, naturally, wine itself add a suitably convivial touch. The best part comes at the top. A panoramic elevator carries visitors up the tower to a lookout offering sweeping views across the surrounding vineyards. The crypt now serves as a community space, making for a more humble spot for eternal rest than some of the other famous players involved in their story (John André, for instance, who was the third conspirator in their plot, is buried quite grandly in the Nave at Westminster). items.title: Ham Ho in Binh Phu, Vietnam
items.summary: Deep within the rugged interior of Tay Son district, Ham Ho presents a striking clash of raw geological wonder and fierce military history. A wild mountain river tears through a colossal maze of jagged granite boulders and dense forest canopy, creating natural stone bridges, hidden waterfalls, and emerald pools that look entirely untouched by time. Beneath its scenic exterior lies a powerful historical secret, as these labyrinthine river channels served as the clandestine training ground for the naval forces of the 18th-century Tay Son uprising. Visitors navigating the rocky waters today can still sense the echoes of a rebellion that once shook the nation. Blending untamed wilderness with the legendary ghosts of Vietnam's most famous peasant army, this river gorge offers an arresting journey into the heart of regional lore.

items.title: Khada Parsi Statue in Mumbai, India
items.summary: In Mumbai’s Byculla area, under the Byculla Bridge, a tall cast-iron statue stands at the traffic junction. It is popularly known as Khada Parsi Statue. It is the statue of Seth Cursetjee Manockjee (1763-1845), a Parsi businessman and philanthropist. The statue was commissioned by his son Mr. Manockjee Cursetjee, as a tribute to his father. According to experts, it is the only cast-iron statue in the city. It was installed in 1867. It is believed that it was the third statue of an Indian person to be built in Mumbai (then Bombay), after the statues of Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy and Jagannath Shankarseth. The statue of Seth Cursetjee Manockjee stands atop a tall Corinthian pillar. At the base of the pillar, there are statues of four mermaids blowing conches, which function as water fountains. items.title: Fort Breendonk in Willebroek, Belgium
items.summary: Fort van Breendonk is a transit camp and WWII Nazi Prison in Willebroek, Belgium. It was originally built between 1906 and 1913 and has been used in both World War I and World War II. It was used as a prison camp for the detention of political prisoners, resistance members, and Jews. It became known for the poor living conditions rather than the many deaths. The camp had more SS guards than prisoners, which meant they were constantly watched. Many prisoners were transported to larger concentration camps in Europe. The fort has held 3,590 prisoners, 303 of whom died in the camp, 1,741 passed away in other camps before the end of the war. The camp was eventually evacuated by September 1944, by the Allies of World War II. items.title: Tomb of Mem de Sá in Salvador, Brazil
items.summary: Located in the heart of Salvador’s historic center, the Catedral Basílica de Salvador stands in the famous Terreiro de Jesus, surrounded by some of the city’s oldest streets and churches. Its richly decorated Baroque interior, covered in intricate carvings, gold details, paintings, and religious artwork, makes it one of the most impressive historic churches in Bahia. What makes the cathedral particularly fascinating is the connection between its beauty and Salvador’s darker colonial history. Inside the church is the sepulchre of Mem de Sá, the third Governor-General of Brazil, who was buried there in the 16th century. His tomb adds an eerie sense of history to the otherwise magnificent interior, reminding visitors that this building has witnessed centuries of political power, religious influence, and colonial life. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us. MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the Universe was about 8 billion years old. items.title: [Comment] Adjuvant radiotherapy for atypical meningioma
items.summary: Surgical resection remains the mainstay of treatment for atypical meningiomas, corresponding to WHO grade 2 tumours, particularly given the substantial risk of recurrence after subtotal resection. Accordingly, adjuvant radiotherapy has been proposed as a means of reducing the risk of recurrence, and its role is relatively well accepted in patients with residual tumour. After gross total resection (defined as Simpson grade I–III), however, the rationale is less clear: 5-year progression-free survival with gross total resection alone is 67–86%, and the role of adjuvant radiotherapy remains controversial, with its benefit in disease control weighed against potential toxicities.

items.title: 14 Real Places That Haunt the Pages of Literature
items.summary: One of literature’s greatest gifts is its ability to transport us to other worlds: some utopian and fantastical, others dark and unnerving, scary and supernatural ... This guide is all about the latter (which are, arguably, much more fun). These are the novels, short stories, and novellas that get under your skin, that stay in your psyche long after you’ve put them down and returned to the world of the living. Little do folks know that many of these works were inspired by — or, in a few cases, explicitly based on — real-life places that you can still visit today. Whether you’re a proud horror nerd or a self-proclaimed scaredy cat, there’s something indescribably special about visiting places that affected authors so deeply they simply had to put them down on paper. items.title: [Articles] Status, challenges, and future directions of machine learning in the management of epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Although machine learning shows promise in predicting epilepsy treatment outcomes, the high heterogeneity and bias—particularly in small sample sizes, handling of missing data, and scarcity of studies with external validation—limit its clinical applicability. Future research should focus on larger, diverse datasets and standardised minimum reporting. Prospective trials are needed to evaluate machine learning models in real-world settings.

items.title: [Review] Machine learning prediction for epilepsy treatment selection and prognosis: achievements and challenges
items.summary: Accurate prediction of treatment response and selection of optimal treatments remain challenging in epilepsy management. With no reliable surrogate biomarkers for treatment response, the current process of selecting an antiseizure medication remains largely a trial-and-error approach. Other non-pharmacological treatment options, such as epilepsy surgery, are viable alternatives for patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. Statistical and machine learning techniques have been used to predict seizure outcomes associated with antiseizure medications and epilepsy surgery.

items.title: [Review] Artificial intelligence models for automated and semiautomated analysis and interpretation of clinical electroencephalography
items.summary: Electroencephalography is the most commonly used diagnostic tool for epilepsy. However, interpreting electroencephalograms (EEGs) requires expertise that is not widely available. Advances in digital technology and wearables have enabled large-scale EEG recording, generating vast amounts of data that cannot be managed through traditional visual interpretation by experts. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to augment human expertise and reduce workloads. The application of artificial neural networks in analysing clinical EEG recordings has led to major breakthroughs, bringing AI-based EEG interpretation closer to clinical implementation.

items.title: Hubble's superbubble scene
items.summary: Image: This sprawling cosmic vista and subject of today’s ESA/Hubble Picture of the Month comes from the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). The LMC is the largest of the small galaxies that orbit our Milky Way galaxy . At just 160 000 light-years away, the LMC offers a close look at highly active stellar birthsites like the nebula shown here. This nebula is named LHA 120-N44, or N44 for short, and it’s located in the constellation Dorado. The appearance of this photogenic nebula is dominated by two features: a vast central void and a shell of dense, dusty gas. The central void is a ‘superbubble’ spanning roughly 210 by 140 light-years. The glittering stars at the centre of the void are responsible for its creation; through their powerful stellar winds and explosive supernovae , these stars have expelled much of the gas from which they were born. items.title: Roman lifts off on a mission to survey the infrared sky
items.summary: Image: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, USA, at 07:26 EDT / 12:26 BST/ 13:26 CEST on 30 August 2026. With the successful launch, Roman began its mission to survey the sky in visible to near-infrared light to help reveal the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The telescope will also investigate the true diversity of exoplanets in our galaxy. Roman is a NASA-led mission to which the European Space Agency (ESA) contributed star trackers, batteries, and detectors for the coronagraph instrument. ESA will also provide communications support through its deep-space ground station network , and enable data download using its new 35-metre antenna in New Norcia, Australia. “I warmly congratulate our colleagues at NASA on the successful launch of Roman,” says Carole Mundell, ESA’s Director of Science.

items.title: Argenx digests phase 2 celiac win for $2.2B drug, preps pivotal run
items.summary: A phase 2 celiac disease trial of argenx’s FB102 has hit its primary endpoint, delivering a boost to a drug candidate that the biotech acquired in its $2.2 billion takeover of Forte Biosciences.

items.title: Cadrenal launches strategic review for late-stage cardiology pipeline
items.summary: Cadrenal Therapeutics, a heart-focused biotech that recently reached an agreement with the FDA on the design of a pivotal trial for its lead candidate, is now instead looking to offload its pipeline or potentially the entire company.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Layoff Tracker 2026: Caribou cuts staff, halts pipeline; Foghorn reduces workforce by 40%
items.summary: As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

items.title: ARPA-H unveils Surpass program to accelerate and expand clinical trials
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced the launch of a new program aimed at removing barriers that slow clinical development and transforming how clinical trials are designed and conducted.

items.title: TCGX launches $600M fund to bankroll Asian biotechs
items.summary: Investment firm TCGX is expanding in Asia, raising $600 million to funnel into biotechs emerging from a burgeoning drug discovery hotspot.

items.title: Cerevance rescues its Parkinson's drug with phase 3 win
items.summary: Cerevance's oral non-dopaminergic therapy has redeemed itself by improving both motor and non-motor symptoms in a phase 3 Parkinson's disease study.

items.title: Atsena’s Lighthouse gene therapy readout illuminates eye disease efficacy
items.summary: Atsena Therapeutics has reported evidence of efficacy in a clinical trial of an eye disease gene therapy, encouraging the biotech to forge ahead with a study that could support a filing for approval in 2028.

items.title: Matchpoint nets $150M series B to take covalent med into clinic
items.summary: Matchpoint Therapeutics has aced its series B round, serving up $150 million to advance the Sanofi-backed biotech’s pipeline of precision covalent medicines.

items.title: MimiVax’s cancer vaccine fails phase 2 glioblastoma study, but CEO still sees data as ‘inspiring’
items.summary: MimiVax has reports a phase 2b miss in newly diagnosed glioblastoma patients, but remains positive about a significant survival benefit in a subset of patients 65 years and under.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker '26: Matchpoint makes $150M; KymaThera corrals $80M
items.summary: The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.

items.title: Abridge, University of Texas System enter enterprise-wide agreement for expanded AI-enabled care
items.summary: The partnership establishes a systemwide framework for the eight UT health institutions to access Abridge.

items.title: Hospital industry sues to block HHS' 340B rebate pilot (again)
items.summary: The American Hospital Association and others have launched a legal rematch with the federal government over the second iteration of a pilot program swapping out safety-net hospitals’ upfront drug discounts for after-the-fact rebates.

items.title: Urban hospitals face closure rates similar to rural facilities, study finds
items.summary: There were 432 acute hospital closures and 216 openings across the country from 2010 through 2025, with the former accelerating over time and the latter slowing, according to a new study. Closure rates were statistically similar between rural and urban hospitals, and generally increased among safety net facilities and for-profits.

items.title: Little room for stakeholder consensus among potential Medicare Advantage reforms
items.summary: A survey of 52 experts spanning researchers, the Medicare Advantage industry, patient advocates and policymakers wasn't able to identify a single policy proposal that would be received wholeheartedly by all three groups.

items.title: CMS: About 71% of MAPD plan enrollees in coverage with four or more stars for 2027
items.summary: The Trump administration has released the 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings, with many enrollees in plans that earned at least four stars.

items.title: HHS launches 4 new vaccine injury research, reporting initiatives
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) on Thursday announced a series of actions aimed at strengthening the federal government's response to vaccine-related health concerns.

items.title: HHS: 340B 'expanded beyond its original intent,' incentivizes consolidation
items.summary: A new brief lays out the administration's views and critiques of the controversial hospital subsidy program, and includes a data analysis suggesting that a proposed reimbursement cut will limit spending growth.

items.title: Chutes & Ladders—WellSpan, Beth Israel Lahey unveil next CEOs
items.summary: Welcome to this week's Chutes & Ladders, our roundup of hirings, firings and retirings throughout the industry. Please submit the good news—or the bad—from your shop, and we will feature it here at the end of each week.

items.title: 'Blue Conspiracy'—Michigan attorney general hits BCBSM with antitrust suit
items.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel has filed suit against Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan, alleging that the insurer operated as a monopoly in the state.

items.title: Fierce Healthcare Fundraising Tracker '26: Outro clinches $7M for deprescribing; Rightway pulls in $155M to expand pharmacy benefits tech
items.summary: Keep up with all the venture capital dollars being funneled into the health tech and digital health industries.

items.title: Suki launches ‘Ask’ feature for clinical decision support driven by Wolters Kluwer UpToDate AI API
items.summary: Ask integrates evidence-based clinical reasoning directly into workflows and can provide answers grounded in UpToDate’s proprietary content.

items.title: Healthleap banks $38M for AI screening platform that catches undiagnosed conditions
items.summary: Healthleap says its platform is the first and only validated AI malnutrition screening tool that contains EHR-integrated screening layers, executives say.

items.title: PhRMA launches new legal challenge as CMS brings 'most favored nation' pricing to Medicare Part B
items.summary: As the Trump administration advances plans to bring its “most favored nation” drug pricing model to Medicare Part B, the pharmaceutical industry’s top lobbying group is pushing back in court.

items.title: Kaiser Permanente to repay nurses 'potentially tens of millions' in mistakenly withheld wages
items.summary: Following an arbitration agreement, more than 1,000 nurses will be compensated for a payment error that began in 2021, the California Nurses Association said. The major nonprofit confirmed the plans but did not comment on the total amount.

items.title: After ICE raids, hospitals saw fewer ED visits, more admissions among foreign-born: study
items.summary: Studies published this week outline changes in care-seeking behavior tied to heightened federal immigration policy and rhetoric, with ramifications for patient outcomes and healthcare spending.

items.title: Cigna unveils new customer experience platform, Health Sense
items.summary: Cigna is rolling out a new patient experience platform that aims to harness the power of data to drive greater personalization.

items.title: General Medicine banks $120M backed by a16z, Eli Lilly and Mercy Health to build out healthcare storefront
items.summary: General Medicine, started by the founding team that built PillPack and Amazon Pharmacy, is an online marketplace where customers can search, compare and buy care, see insurance and cash prices before deciding, and get guidance from a licensed clinician.

items.title: Utah expands healthcare AI sandbox with August AI, Nolla Health pilots, adds third-party evaluators
items.summary: Utah is expanding the state's AI regulatory sandbox program with new pilots to test AI-supported prescription renewals, dermatology and physical therapy, while adding physician oversight and independent third-party evaluators.

items.title: Senators question Kennedy on 'major break' from USPSTF appointment norms
items.summary: The lawmakers expressed concerns over the panel’s ability to make recommendations, the transparency of the application process and more.

items.title: The future of independent contracting in healthcare
items.summary: More clinicians are turning to independent contracting for greater flexibility, but uncertainty around worker classification can complicate those arrangements. This week on "Podnosis," Senior Writer Anastassia Gliadkovskaya talks with ShiftKey’s Regan Parker about the Department of Labor’s proposed independent contractor rule, portable benefits and what the future of independent contracting could look like in healthcare.

items.title: NIH launches $21 million initiative to improve understanding of sex-specific hormonal biology
items.summary: Program will use new approaches in computational modeling for deeper investigations into how sex influences treatment response.
